title: add-jsonschema-response_format-strict-mode-and-improved-errors-openai-compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add response_format=json_schema support; implement strict mode for JSON schema validation with improved OpenAI-compatible error messages; SDKs accept response_format parameter and surface validation errors in a stable format; docs + migration notes added.
description: Context: Add first-class JSON schema structured output support to the API surface via the response_format parameter and enable a strict validation mode that returns clear, OpenAI-compatible error objects when model output violates the schema. Motivation: customers rely on predictable structured outputs for downstream parsers. Previously we had ad-hoc schema helpers; this PR formalizes the contract at the API gateway and OpenAI-compat layer and improves runtime validation errors so customer apps can react deterministically. What this changes: 1) API accepts response_format=json_schema with a top-level schema blob (or reference to a registered schema) and optional strict=true flag. 2) The OpenAI compatibility layer maps existing response_format usage to our internal structured-output pipeline so existing clients using the compatibility endpoint see the same behavior. 3) A validation step runs against the final text->json parse; in strict mode we run JSON Schema Draft-07 validation and return a structured error payload consistent with OpenAI-style errors (error.type = "invalid_response_format", message, details including json_path and validator keyword). 4) Non-strict mode now includes a best-effort repair attempt (trim/normalize) and returns a warning field if repaired. Implementation notes: - Added api/router changes to accept response_format payload and pass metadata to the inference runtime. - Implemented server-side JSON schema validator module (go/service/structured_output/validator.go) with pluggable validator backend for future schema versions. - Extended openai_compat adapter to translate our validation errors into the compatibility error envelope so downstream SDKs see the same shape. - Added end-to-end tests: unit validators, integration tests with model output mocking, and an e2e scenario exercising strict failures. - Updated Python/TS SDK shims to accept the new response_format parameter shape and bubble up structured validation errors. Backwards compatibility: If response_format is not provided, behavior is unchanged. The new fields are opt-in. Migration: customers using custom parsing should switch to response_format=json_schema and enable strict=true after validating on dev traffic. Checklist: - [x] API contract and schema for response_format documented - [x] Implement validation + error mapping - [x] SDK surface updates (python/typescript) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Benchmarked latency impact (tight loop + cache; <2ms median per-request overhead)

notes_on_backward_compat: Behavior is opt-in. Existing clients without response_format continue to receive freeform text. The compatibility layer accepts both the legacy response_format usage and the new json_schema shape. No migration required unless strict enforcement is desired.
